note: This is the alpha-equivalence of bound variables. The proof assistant handles it. It is not a statement.

quote: yielding $e(\blank)$ as alternative notation for the function $x \mapsto e(x)$.
note: This is the underscore notation for anonymous functions. It is only notation.

quote: The notation $b \jdeq c$ will denote the statement that the expressions $b$ and $c$ become the same thing …
note: This is the meta-level definitional equality (and \defeq for definitions). It corresponds to the judgmental equality of Narya. It is not an internal statement.

quote: We define the \emph{composite} function $g \circ f : X \to Z$ by setting $g \circ f \defeq (a \mapsto g(f(a)))$.

note: Narya has one Type : Type. The formalization models a universe as a small-predicate with closure fields. It also has nested pairs U : U' with cumulativity. There is no hierarchy U_0 : U_1 : … and no designated smallest U_0.

quote: It follows from the properties above that there are an infinite number of universes, for each one is an element of a larger one.
note: This is a metatheoretic claim about the ambient hierarchy. Narya has Type : Type (total_universe contains its own type). Thus a faithful statement of the claim is not possible.

quote: The flexibility offered by this correspondence between families of types in $\UU$ and functions to $\UU$ will often be used.

quote: Here are Peano's rules for constructing the natural numbers in the form that is used in type theory.

quote: that different natural numbers have different successors; and that no number has $0$ as its successor. Those omitted rules remain true
